### CPU memory map

| Range | Size | Region | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$00-$7FFF` | 32,768 | `BASE_RAM` | 32 KiB of RAM, always present: zero page, stack, system pages, the kernel image and the start of BASIC's workspace. |
| `$8000-$BFFF` | 16,384 | `EXTENDED_RAM_WINDOW` | 16 KiB window into 512 KiB of banked RAM; VIA Port A PA0-PA4 select one of 32 banks. |
| `$C000-$DFFF` | 8,192 | `IO` | Eight 1 KiB device slots. |
| `$E000-$FFFF` | 8,192 | `MIA` | MIA is selected for the whole region but sees only A0-A4: its 32 registers at $FFE0-$FFFF repeat every 32 bytes below. A mirror is the same register, side effects included; programs use $FFE0-$FFFF only. |

I/O slots:

| Range | Select | Device | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$C000-$C3FF` | `IOCS0` | 65C22 VIA | Port A drives extended RAM banking; Port B, CA1/CA2 and CB1/CB2 go to the user port header. Registers repeat every 16 bytes. |
| `$C400-$C7FF` | `IOCS1` | free | Free slot on the expansion headers; a card claims it by jumpering this select line. |
| `$C800-$CBFF` | `IOCS2` | free | Free slot on the expansion headers; a card claims it by jumpering this select line. |
| `$CC00-$CFFF` | `IOCS3` | free | Free slot on the expansion headers; a card claims it by jumpering this select line. |
| `$D000-$D3FF` | `IOCS4` | free | Free slot on the expansion headers; a card claims it by jumpering this select line. |
| `$D400-$D7FF` | `IOCS5` | free | Free slot on the expansion headers; a card claims it by jumpering this select line. |
| `$D800-$DBFF` | `IOCS6` | free | Free slot on the expansion headers; a card claims it by jumpering this select line. |
| `$DC00-$DFFF` | `IOCS7` | free | Free slot on the expansion headers; a card claims it by jumpering this select line. |

VIA registers (repeating every 16 bytes in slot 0):

| Address | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$C000` | `VIA_ORB` | Port B data. Free: Port B goes to the user port header. |
| `$C001` | `VIA_ORA` | Port A data. PA0-PA4 select the extended RAM bank; PA5-PA7 are unused by the system. |
| `$C002` | `VIA_DDRB` | Port B direction. Free. |
| `$C003` | `VIA_DDRA` | Port A direction. The kernel sets PA0-PA4 as outputs. |
| `$C004` | `VIA_T1CL` | Timer 1 counter low. The kernel's: reading it clears Timer 1's interrupt. |
| `$C005` | `VIA_T1CH` | Timer 1 counter high. The kernel's: writing it starts the timer. |
| `$C006` | `VIA_T1LL` | Timer 1 latch low. The kernel loads 6250 (VIA_T1_RELOAD). |
| `$C007` | `VIA_T1LH` | Timer 1 latch high. The kernel's. |
| `$C008` | `VIA_T2CL` | Timer 2 counter low. Free. |
| `$C009` | `VIA_T2CH` | Timer 2 counter high. Free. |
| `$C00A` | `VIA_SR` | Shift register. Free. |
| `$C00B` | `VIA_ACR` | Auxiliary control. The kernel owns bits 7-6 (Timer 1 free-running, PB7 output off) and keeps bits 5-0 as it finds them. |
| `$C00C` | `VIA_PCR` | Peripheral control (CA1/CA2, CB1/CB2). Free. |
| `$C00D` | `VIA_IFR` | Interrupt flags. The kernel's IRQ handler checks bit 6 (Timer 1); other sources are free. |
| `$C00E` | `VIA_IER` | Interrupt enable. The kernel enables only Timer 1, at reset and at warm start, which turn every other source off. |
| `$C00F` | `VIA_ORA_NH` | Port A data without handshake. Same pins as ORA, so PA0-PA4 still select the bank. |

Zero page (`$0000-$00FF`):

| Range | Block | Owner | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$00-$97` | `BASIC` | basic | BASIC's variables and its CHRGET routine. A program that replaces BASIC may use them. |
| `$98-$DF` | `PROGRAMS` | programs | Free for programs (72 bytes). BASIC, WozMon and the kernel never touch them, so code called with SYS or USR can keep state here. |
| `$E0-$E7` | `SYSTEM_SPARE` | system | Spare for the system, next to the programs' block so it can be handed to programs later. |
| `$E8-$EF` | `WOZMON` | wozmon | WozMon's variables, used only while it runs. Outside BASIC's block, so MON keeps the program. |
| `$F0-$FF` | `KERNEL` | kernel | Kernel variables. Programs that replace BASIC still leave them alone: the IRQ updates KJIFFY and KERN_LOAD takes its parameters in KPTR/KTMP. |

| Address | Size | Name | Owner | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$00` | 3 | `GORESTART` | basic | JMP to BASIC's warm restart (RESTART), written at cold start. |
| `$03` | 3 | `GOSTROUT` | basic | JMP to STROUT, which prints the string at A/Y. |
| `$06` | 2 | `GOAYINT` | basic | Address of AYINT (FAC to a 16-bit integer), for machine code called through USR. |
| `$08` | 2 | `GOGIVEAYF` | basic | Address of GIVAYF (the 16-bit integer in A/Y to FAC), for machine code called through USR. |
| `$0A` | 3 | `USR` | basic | JMP to the routine USR() calls. Cold start points it at the ILLEGAL QUANTITY error; POKE a routine's address into $0B-$0C. |
| `$0D` | 1 | `Z15` | basic | msbasic's NULL count. This build has no NULL command, so nothing reads or writes it. |
| `$0E` | 1 | `POSX` | basic | Output column BASIC tracks for TAB, SPC, POS and comma zones. |
| `$0F` | 1 | `Z17` | basic | Line width, set to 40 at cold start. Only the CR-at-width code reads it, and this build leaves that code out (CONFIG_NO_CR). |
| `$10` | 1 | `Z18` | basic | Last column where a comma starts a new print zone, set to 14 at cold start. Unused for the same reason as Z17. |
| `$11` | 2 | `LINNUM`, `TXPSV` | basic | 16-bit integer result: a line number, or the address PEEK, POKE and SYS take. |
| `$13` | 1 | `CHARAC` | basic | Delimiter the scanner stops at (string literals, DATA items). |
| `$14` | 1 | `ENDCHR` | basic | Second delimiter for the same scans. |
| `$15` | 1 | `EOLPNTR` | basic | Index into the input buffer while tokenizing; subscript count while building an array. |
| `$16` | 1 | `DIMFLG` | basic | Nonzero while DIM creates an array. |
| `$17` | 2 | `VALTYP` | basic | Type of the last expression: byte 0 is $FF for a string, $00 for a number; byte 1 is $80 for an integer. |
| `$19` | 1 | `DATAFLG` | basic | Tokenizer flag set after DATA, so the rest of the statement is not crunched. LIST uses it for its quote state. |
| `$1A` | 1 | `SUBFLG` | basic | Flag that forbids subscripts or integers (FN parameters, FOR variables). |
| `$1B` | 1 | `INPUTFLG` | basic | Which statement is reading values: INPUT, GET or READ. |
| `$1C` | 1 | `CPRMASK` | basic | Relational operator mask a comparison tests its result against. SIN and TAN reuse it as a sign flag. |
| `$1D` | 1 | `Z14` | basic | Output-suppress flag (CTRL-O). Kept just below TEMPPT; see defines_clementina.s. |
| `$1E` | 1 | `TEMPPT` | basic | Zero page address of the next free descriptor in TEMPST. |
| `$1F` | 2 | `LASTPT` | basic | Pointer to the last temporary string descriptor used. |
| `$21` | 9 | `TEMPST` | basic | Temporary string descriptor stack: three 3-byte descriptors. |
| `$2A` | 2 | `INDEX` | basic | General pointer (string moves, variable search, memory moves). |
| `$2C` | 2 | `DEST` | basic | Second general pointer, mostly a move destination. |
| `$2E` | 5 | `RESULT` | basic | Work area for floating-point multiply and divide. |
| `$33` | 2 | `TXTTAB` | basic | Start of the BASIC program text. |
| `$35` | 2 | `VARTAB` | basic | Start of simple variables, right after the program. |
| `$37` | 2 | `ARYTAB` | basic | Start of arrays. |
| `$39` | 2 | `STREND` | basic | End of arrays plus one, the bottom of free memory. |
| `$3B` | 2 | `FRETOP` | basic | Bottom of string storage, which grows down from MEMSIZ. |
| `$3D` | 2 | `FRESPC` | basic | Pointer to the string most recently allocated. |
| `$3F` | 2 | `MEMSIZ` | basic | Top of BASIC memory plus one ($C000 at cold start). Lower it with POKE 63/64 and CLEAR to reserve RAM. |
| `$41` | 2 | `CURLIN` | basic | Line number being run; high byte $FF in direct mode. |
| `$43` | 2 | `OLDLIN` | basic | Line number where the program stopped, for CONT. |
| `$45` | 2 | `OLDTEXT` | basic | Text pointer where the program stopped, for CONT. |
| `$47` | 2 | `Z8C` | basic | Line number of the DATA statement being read, for READ's errors. |
| `$49` | 2 | `DATPTR` | basic | Address of the next DATA item READ takes. |
| `$4B` | 2 | `INPTR` | basic | Where INPUT, GET and READ are reading from. |
| `$4D` | 2 | `VARNAM` | basic | Name of the variable being looked up (two characters, type in bit 7). |
| `$4F` | 2 | `VARPNT` | basic | Address of that variable's value. |
| `$51` | 2 | `FORPNT` | basic | Pointer to the variable a FOR, LET or INPUT assigns. |
| `$53` | 2 | `LASTOP` | basic | Operator table offset of the operator pending during expression evaluation. |
| `$55` | 1 | `CPRTYP` | basic | Relational operators (<, =, >) collected while a comparison is parsed. |
| `$56` | 2 | `TEMP3`, `FNCNAM` | basic | Pointer to the current FN definition; also scratch. |
| `$58` | 3 | `DSCPTR` | basic | Pointer to the current string descriptor. |
| `$5B` | 2 | `DSCLEN`, `JMPADRS` | basic | Descriptor step during garbage collection (3 at cold start). Its second byte starts JMPADRS. |
| `$5D` | 1 | `Z52` | basic | Garbage collection: copy of DSCLEN, the step between the descriptors being scanned. Also the low byte of JMPADRS's target. |
| `$5E` | 1 | `ARGEXTENSION` | basic | Extra low mantissa byte of ARG. Also the high byte of JMPADRS's target. |
| `$5F` | 1 | `TEMP1` | basic | Floating-point scratch. |
| `$60` | 2 | `HIGHDS` | basic | Block move: end of the destination. |
| `$62` | 2 | `HIGHTR` | basic | Block move: end of the source. |
| `$64` | 1 | `TEMP2` | basic | Floating-point scratch. |
| `$65` | 1 | `INDX`, `TMPEXP` | basic | Floating-point scratch: an index or a temporary exponent. |
| `$66` | 1 | `EXPON` | basic | Decimal exponent while a number is parsed. |
| `$67` | 1 | `LOWTR`, `LOWTRX` | basic | Low byte of a pointer used by line search and block moves; EXPSGN is its high byte. |
| `$68` | 1 | `EXPSGN` | basic | Sign of the decimal exponent while a number is parsed. |
| `$69` | 5 | `FAC` | basic | Floating-point accumulator: exponent, then four mantissa bytes. |
| `$6E` | 1 | `FACSIGN` | basic | Sign of FAC. |
| `$6F` | 1 | `SERLEN` | basic | Number of terms left while a polynomial series is evaluated. |
| `$70` | 1 | `SHIFTSIGNEXT` | basic | Sign extension while mantissas are shifted; zero after cold start. |
| `$71` | 5 | `ARG` | basic | Second floating-point accumulator, same layout as FAC. |
| `$76` | 1 | `ARGSIGN` | basic | Sign of ARG. |
| `$77` | 2 | `STRNG1`, `SGNCPR`, `FACEXTENSION` | basic | String pointer. Its first byte is SGNCPR (FAC and ARG signs compared), its second FACEXTENSION (FAC's rounding byte). |
| `$79` | 2 | `STRNG2` | basic | Second string pointer. |
| `$7B` | 24 | `CHRGET`, `CHRGOT`, `TXTPTR`, `CHRGOT2` | basic | Routine cold start copies here: steps TXTPTR and returns the next non-space character. CHRGOT ($81) rereads the current one. |
| `$93` | 5 | `RNDSEED` | basic | Seed RND works from, in FAC layout. Cold start copies only its first four bytes (an msbasic quirk noted in init.s). |
| `$E8` | 1 | `XAML` | wozmon | Low byte of the last opened address. |
| `$E9` | 1 | `XAMH` | wozmon | High byte of the last opened address. |
| `$EA` | 1 | `STL` | wozmon | Low byte of the store address. |
| `$EB` | 1 | `STH` | wozmon | High byte of the store address. |
| `$EC` | 1 | `L` | wozmon | Low byte of the hex value being parsed. |
| `$ED` | 1 | `H` | wozmon | High byte of the hex value being parsed. |
| `$EE` | 1 | `YSAV` | wozmon | Saved input index, to see whether a hex value was typed. |
| `$EF` | 1 | `MODE` | wozmon | Command mode: $00 examine, $7F store, $AE block examine. |
| `$F0` | 2 | `KPTR` | kernel | General 16-bit pointer: PRSTR's string source, KERN_LOAD's destination override. CHROUT leaves it alone. |
| `$F2` | 2 | `KTMP` | kernel | Scratch: the overlay offset and address CHROUT computes. KERN_LOAD takes its run address here when it jumps; 0 means the first byte loaded. |
| `$F4` | 2 | `KCNT` | kernel | 16-bit loop counter for screen fills. |
| `$F6` | 1 | `KCHR` | kernel | CHROUT's copy of the byte being printed. |
| `$F7` | 2 | `KJIFFY` | kernel | Free-running tick counter, +1 per VIA Timer 1 IRQ (PHI2 / 6250, 192 Hz at 1.2 MHz). Measures CPU work, not wall time. Read-only for programs. |
| `$F9` | 1 | `KLOAD_BANK` | kernel | KERN_LOAD: the bank being written at $8000-$BFFF. |
| `$FA` | 1 | `KLOAD_CHUNKLEN` | kernel | KERN_LOAD: bytes read this round. |
| `$FB` | 1 | `KLOAD_SCRATCH` | kernel | KERN_LOAD: header and boundary scratch. |
| `$FC` | 4 |  | kernel | Spare. The kernel grows into these first, then into $E0-$E7. |

Stack (`$0100-$01FF`):

| Range | Block | Owner | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$0100-$01FB` | `CPU_STACK` | cpu | 6502 hardware stack. Cold start sets S to $FF; while BASIC runs S stays at or below $FC, so pushes reach $01FC at most. |
| `$01FC-$01FF` | `BASIC_LINE_STAGING` | basic | BASIC stages a numbered line's link and line number here, just below its input buffer. |

| Address | Size | Name | Owner | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$01FC` | 2 |  | basic | Staged link of a numbered line (INPUTBUFFER-4). The high byte is set to $01 before the copy; the low byte is a don't-care, and BASIC's deepest push lands on it. |
| `$01FE` | 2 |  | basic | Staged line number (INPUTBUFFER-2), copied from LINNUM. INPUT stores its leading comma at $01FF. |

Input page (`$0200-$02FF`):

| Range | Block | Owner | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$0200-$027F` | `LINE_INPUT` | basic,wozmon | Line input buffer, shared by BASIC and WozMon, which never run at the same time. |
| `$0280-$02F7` | `PROGRAMS` | programs | Free for programs (120 bytes). Nothing in the system writes here. |
| `$02F8-$02FF` | `CLOCK_SNAPSHOT` | kernel | Copy of MIA's clock written by KERN_RDTIM, in the layout MIA latches at $11078. BASIC's TI, TICKS and DELAY overwrite it too. |

| Address | Size | Name | Owner | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$0200` | 83 | `INPUTBUFFER` | basic | Typed line, up to 80 characters (INLIN_MAX), crunched in place; $00 terminator at $0250 and the tokenizer's end-of-program $00 at most at $0252. GET uses $0200-$0201. |
| `$0200` | 128 | `IN` | wozmon | WozMon's line buffer. |
| `$02F8` | 4 | `CLOCK_MS` | kernel | Milliseconds since MIA reset, little-endian, wraps at 2^32 (about 49.7 days). |
| `$02FC` | 3 | `CLOCK_60HZ` | kernel | MIA's 60 Hz count, little-endian, wraps at 5,184,000 (24 hours). BASIC's TI reads it; KERN_SETTIM sets it. |
| `$02FF` | 1 | `CLOCK_VERSION` | kernel | 1 when MIA filled the snapshot. |
